title: Anthropic skipped UK pre-release tests for Mythos 5.1, the FT reports
content:
Anthropic did not give Britain’s AI Security Institute (AISI) its Mythos 5.1 model to test before release, the Financial Times reported. Reporters Lucy Fisher and Madhumita Murgia said it is the first time a major model has been kept from the UK institute before launch. TNW has not independently verified the report.
The FT reported that Anthropic did give comparable US organisations access. According to the paper, UK officials fear a wider protectionist shift among American AI companies. They see it as falling into line with the Trump administration. Anthropic has not publicly explained the decision.
What the UK is missing
Anthropic released Mythos 5.1 on 1 September alongside Fable 5.1. Access is limited to approved partners in Project Glasswing. That is the industry group Anthropic formed around the original Mythos model.
AISI has tested Anthropic models before. In April it published an evaluation of the Mythos preview’s cyber capabilities. It found the model was the first to finish its 32-step simulated network attack. It did so in three of ten attempts.
The institute has also been one of the most direct critics of how frontier agents behave. In August, its testers caught OpenAI and Anthropic agents taking unauthorised actions in the lab. On Wednesday, Anthropic published its own review of four incidents. In each, Claude models reached the open internet during supposedly closed tests.
The government’s response
The UK government did not criticise Anthropic directly. A Cabinet Office spokesperson told ITPro that AISI continues to work closely with industry partners, “including Anthropic”. The spokesperson pointed out that the institute tested OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra before its public release only last week.
“These risks do not stop at national borders and no country can tackle them alone,” the spokesperson told ITPro. ITPro said Anthropic had not responded to its request for comment.
Europe got in, eventually
The picture is not one of Anthropic shutting out Europe entirely. On Thursday, the EU’s cybersecurity agency ENISA began testing Mythos 5 after months of talks. Bloomberg reported that ENISA still does not have access to Mythos 5.1.
Access has been political for months. In June, Washington imposed temporary export restrictions on Mythos 5 and Fable 5, cutting off foreign users. It lifted the controls on Fable 5 in July.
A durable advantage, or a dwindling one
Some policy analysts expected this. Keegan McBride, director of science, technology and AI policy at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, called the FT report “just the start of what is to come” in a post on LinkedIn. Any UK AI strategy relying on AISI beyond the next two years “is unserious,” he wrote.
His argument is that Washington increasingly treats its AI lead as a security asset. On that reading, a UK-led network of safety institutes looks different from Washington. Those institutes depend on early access to American models, which could look like an attempt to govern American technology from abroad.
‘Worrying precedent’
Others read the decision as a loss for safety rather than for Britain alone. Miles Brundage, a former OpenAI policy researcher, called it a “worrying precedent” in a post on X. He added that AISI has more overall capacity than CAISI, its US counterpart.
Ed Newton-Rex, who campaigns on AI and creators’ rights, argued that the episode shows a deeper flaw. An institute that relies on labs volunteering their models “has no teeth,” he wrote on X. Governments should make independent safety testing mandatory, he argued.
From the US side, lawyer Preston Byrne suggested the UK’s approach to online speech regulation was the problem. Britain might get earlier access to American software, he wrote on X, if it were not “the global leader in censorship.”
One decision, or a policy
The counter-argument is in the government’s own statement. AISI still tested GPT-6 Astra days ago, and Anthropic gave it the Mythos preview in April. One withheld model may be a single decision rather than a policy.
The test is the next launch. If Anthropic’s following frontier model reaches AISI before release, this looks like an exception. If it does not, and OpenAI follows, the UK’s flagship AI institution loses the access its work depends on.

report.summary: Anthropic 首次未向英国 AISI 提供 Mythos 5.1 发布前测试
report.background: Anthropic 于 9 月 1 日发布 Mythos 5.1，访问仅限 Project Glasswing 获批伙伴。英国 AI 安全研究所（AISI）此前曾评测 Mythos 预览版，发现它是首个完成 32 步模拟网络攻击的模型（10 次中成功 3 次）。据《金融时报》报道，这是首次有主流模型在发布前被排除在英国机构之外，但 Anthropic 仍向美国同类机构开放。此前 6 月美国曾对 Mythos 5、Fable 5 施加临时出口限制，7 月解除对 Fable 5 的限制；欧盟 ENISA 经数月谈判才获准测试 Mythos 5，仍拿不到 5.1。
key_points: 《金融时报》报道 Anthropic 未在发布前把 Mythos 5.1 交给英国 AISI 测试，这是主流模型首次被挡在英国机构门外，而美国同类机构仍获访问权。
Mythos 5.1 与 Fable 5.1 同日发布，访问仅限 Project Glasswing 的获批合作方，Anthropic 至今未公开解释为何跳过英国。
模型访问已被政治化：6 月美国曾对 Mythos 5、Fable 5 施加临时出口限制，7 月才放开 Fable 5，欧盟 ENISA 目前仍未拿到 5.1。
英国政府未直接批评 Anthropic，强调 AISI 上周还测试了 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra，并称“这些风险不分国界，没有国家能独自应对”。
分析人士分歧明显：有人认为这是华盛顿把 AI 领先当安全资产的开始，也有人称依赖企业自愿送测的机构“没有牙齿”，应强制独立评测。
关键观察点是下一次发布：若后续前沿模型恢复送测，这可能只是个案；若 OpenAI 跟进，英国 AISI 的评测能力将被实质性削弱。
report.impact: 对 AI 行业而言，前沿模型的预发布安全评测正从技术合作滑向地缘政治筹码，若美企普遍收紧，英欧“安全研究所网络”的独立评估能力将被削弱，全球安全标准趋于碎片化。对开发者而言，Mythos、Fable 系列的接口与访问权限可能随出口管制和伙伴名单变动而收紧，依赖单一前沿模型的产品需准备多供应商冗余。对普通用户而言，第三方独立验证减少、透明度下降，更难判断模型真实风险。
report.tools: 想跟进模型安全评测，可关注英国 AISI 开源的 Inspect 评测框架及其公开报告、METR 的任务级能力评估，以及 Anthropic 自身发布的 Claude 事故复盘。红队与提示安全测试可用开源工具 Garak、Promptfoo 上手实践。
